items.title: The latest on FedRAMP 20x Phase 4
items.text:
This site is under development. :)

It shouldn't be public, but if you've stumbled across it, please stand by.

FedRAMP 20x Phase 4 is a 9-month pilot and development phase intended to transition all new commercial FedRAMP Certifications to FedRAMP 20x. It began on October 1, 2026 (FY27 Q1) and will run through June 30, 2027 (FY27 Q3).

At the completion of Phase 4, FedRAMP 20x will move into Phase 5 which will focus on creating a transition path for legacy Rev5 Certifications.

items.title: 20x Class D Pilot
items.text:
Developing and testing assurance requirements for FedRAMP 20x Class D (High). The 20x Class D Pilot will start in January 2027 and is open to participants with a FedRAMP 20x Class C Certification who are selected by FedRAMP based on qualifications shown in a special application.

20x Class D Pilot

items.title: 20x Self-Hosted Rules
items.text:
Collaborating with industry to identify effective existing commercial certifications and requirements that can be reused for self-hosted or hybrid-hosted services as an alternative to a traditional control-based approach for managing physical datacenter infrastructure.

20x Self-Hosted

items.title: Rev5 Program Closeout
items.text:
New FedRAMP Rev5 Certification won't be available after June 11, 2027, so FedRAMP will initiate a special project in early 2027 to ensure that any cloud service offering that is in process with an agency sponsor for Rev5 can receive a FedRAMP Certification before the pipeline officially closes.

Rev5 Program Closeout

items.title: Agency Cloud Use Pilot
items.text:
Developing and testing the new FedRAMP Board-approved Cloud Authorization Management Framework and Cloud Security Authorization process with agencies - for both FedRAMP Rev5 and 20x.

Agency Cloud Use Pilot

items.title: A-130 Class G Pilot
items.text:
Working with agencies to implement government-specific expectations for agency-provided cloud service offerings created by government, for government.

A-130 Class G Pilot

items.title: The 20x Class D Cloud-Hosted Pilot
items.text:
The 20x Class D Cloud-Hosted Pilot is an industry-facing initiative.

Pilot Objective: Develop additional FedRAMP 20x requirements to increase continuous ongoing assurance to a level roughly equivalent with the one-time assurance from a FedRAMP Rev5 Class D Certification, adjusted to account for modern changes in expectations.

items.title: Background
items.text:
FedRAMP 20x Certifications were initially developed for historical Low then Moderate equivalent FedRAMP Certifications, but the push into Class D begins now.

Learn more at Background

items.title: Schedule
items.text:
The 20x Class D Pilot officially begins in January 2027 with the expectation that interested cloud services apply in early January, develop a draft pilot package by late March, and submit a final package by the end of May.

Learn more at Schedule

items.title: Participation
items.text:
Formal participation in the pilot is limited to companies that have applied for a FedRAMP 20x Class C Certification and present a successful pilot proposal to FedRAMP. Cloud services can always follow along with the Class D Pilot activities in public even if they don't make it into the formal pilot!

Learn more at Participation

items.title: Who's In
items.text:
It's always helpful to know who is actively participating in a formal way and learn a bit more about why they chose to participate.

Learn more at Who's In

items.text:
The 20x Class D Cloud-Hosted Rules build on the existing 20x Class C rules. The rules are primarily available in a machine-readable format with a human-readable version showing the differences generated for this web page.

items.title: 20x Class D Pilot Participation
items.text:
Participation in the 20x Class D Pilot will be restricted to maximize efficiency and decrease risk. Cloud services are eligible to apply for participation in the 20x Class D Pilot if they meet the following criteria:

  1. The cloud service offering applied for a FedRAMP 20x Class C Certification before December 11, 2026.
  2. The FedRAMP 20x Class C application is complete and sufficient, addressing all applicable requirements with appropriate implementations.
  3. The FedRAMP 20x Class C application includes a broadly supportive independent verification and validation that is also complete and sufficient.
  4. Agree to implement all FedRAMP 20x Class D Pilot requirements with independent verification and validation by May 7, 2027.

items.title: Application
items.text:
Eligible cloud service offerings will be able to apply to participate in the 20x Class D Pilot in the beginning of January 2027. Application will require a presentation to FedRAMP demonstrating the readiness and executive support necessary to complete a 20x Class D Certification in the time alloted.

Interested and eligible providers should carefully review the entire application process and discuss it internally prior to applying.

items.title: Application Form
items.text:
FedRAMP will provide an application form in early December that will allow cloud service providers to sign up and prove eligibility. This form will require:

  • Cloud service metadata including name, offering name, FedRAMP ID, etc.
  • Name, title, and contact information for primary point of contact
  • Email address for a distribution list managed by the cloud service provider for ongoing comms (we will not maintain lists of a bunch of email addresses to include on communications)

FedRAMP will review this information and contact you to schedule a Pilot Proposal.

items.title: Pilot Proposals
items.text:
Pilot Proposals were a highlight of the FedRAMP 20x Phase 2 pilot, so we are bringing them back with minor changes! Pilot Proposals help FedRAMP get to know you, learn about your company, and make an informed estimate of your ability to meet the requirements while providing meaningful feedback that will benefit FedRAMP and all other stakeholders. They also publicly demonstrate commitment and support up front because you'll need to agree to FedRAMP sharing the proposal with the community.

For 20x Phase 4 Class D Pilot Proposals, we expect each company to bring the following participants:

  • A senior executive sponsor (they don't have to present but we want to know you have the juice).
  • Your GRC engineering and federal compliance team or equivalent (at least the senior folks).
  • A representative from your independent assessment service (more than one is even better) - unlike the Phase 2 pilot proposals, the assessor will not be required to present but this is still an opportunity to showcase a strong working relationship.

The FedRAMP Team

You can expect to be presenting to the FedRAMP Director (Pete), Security Director (Nicole), Chief of Staff (Ryan), Vanguard 20x Team Lead (Dan), and maybe a few other folks on the FedRAMP team.

Be ready for both technical and non-technical questions from FedRAMP!

items.title: Pilot Proposal Content
items.text:
You will need to present the following information aligned with these general timelines:

  1. Introduction and Background (~15 minutes)
    • Introduce your team, including your assessor, and say hello!
    • Provide a brief overview of your cloud service and history with FedRAMP.
    • Explain why you want to participate in the 20x Class D pilot, and why you are confident in providing that level of assurance to the government.
    • Tell us about your GRC environment, including a quick review of tools you are using vs building yourself.
  2. Class D Pilot Approach (~30 minutes)
    • Demonstrate how you plan to approach each of the new Key Security Indicators.
    • Discuss any Class D-specific rules that you think are particularly interesting and how you will approach them.
  3. Q&A w/ FedRAMP (~10 minutes)
    • The FedRAMP team will ask follow-up questions based on your proposal.

There is no template slide deck, specific order of approach for KSIs etc., or any such rigid structure. You should design this presentation to convey information most effectively for your service.

Don't worry too much about perfect presentation but do plan it out!

You won't be judged primarily on the quality and polish of your presentation, but we do want to see that you're taking this seriously and investing time and effort into the process. We strongly recommend that you practice as a team and get feedback from folks within your company (and maybe your assessor!) to smooth off any sharp edges so that the team is confident and ready to go on proposal day.

There's a good chance we'll have proposals or other meetings scheduled back-to-back, so keep an eye on the clock and make sure you don't run over or we'll miss out on critical information!

This is not a sales pitch!

We don't really care about what your cloud service itself does, and we don't want to hear about that in depth. You are certainly welcome to talk about it in your introduction but we expect the majority of the proposal to focus on how you will approach the pilot.

This applies even for GRC tools - we don't want to hear about how your GRC tool works or what it will do, we want to hear about the technical and philosophical approach you will bring to using it.

items.text: 20x Self/Hybrid-Hosted Rules Development is an industry-facing initiative.

items.title: Background
items.text:
FedRAMP 20x originally focused on cloud-hosted services so expanding coverage to self-hosted and hybrid-hosted services requires the development of a new approach to including assessment of the security of datacenter infrastructure and physical environments into a FedRAMP 20x Certification.

Learn more at Background

items.title: Schedule
items.text:
The development of 20x Self/Hybrid-Hosted rules will take place throughout 20x Phase 4, with public Requests For Comment and direct engagement with industry stakeholders.

Learn more at Schedule

items.title: Participation
items.text:
Anyone will be able to participate in Requests For Comment and other public engagements, but some cloud service providers and independent assessment services that meet specific criteria will also have the opportunity to share their experience directly with FedRAMP.

items.title: 20x Self/Hybrid-Hosted Rules Development
items.text:
this is incomplete

To enable maximum speed and widest adoption, FedRAMP 20x Phase 1-3 focused exclusively on developing an updated path for cloud services that were hosted on infrastructure or platforms that were already FedRAMP Rev5 Certified. This provided a path for the majority of cloud services, but de-prioritized a path for the rare services that operate their own physical infrastructure.

FedRAMP plans to remedy this in the Consolidated Rules for 2027 by offering an expanded set of criteria for self-hosted or hybrid-hosted services to qualify for a FedRAMP 20x Certification of any Class. We understand that most companies who are responsible for their own infrastructure are already expected or required to meet stringent government regulations and commercial guidelines to operate datacenters safely. We anticipate leveraging those existing investments to the maximum extent possible.

There is now a single Industry Engagement track for Phase 4.

RFC-0033 Phase 4 Development Tracks for 20x Class D initially proposed 2 separate industry engagement tracks, one for cloud service providers and another for independent assessment services. We have reworked this into a single Industry Engagement track to ensure all activities align with the same schedule.

During Phase 4, FedRAMP will gather data and perspectives directly from current FedRAMP Certified cloud service providers with self-hosted or hybrid-hosted services and their independent assessment services. We will focus on industry standard certifications that are most widely used by these providers, and the deltas between those certifications and the requirements from existing FedRAMP Rev5. Our goal, where possible, will be to identify existing reusable certifications and classifications that can be included directly in a FedRAMP 20x Certification to address infrastructure-related controls.

FedRAMP will also publish at least 2 RFCs related to self-hosted and hybrid-hosted rules to ensure all stakeholders have the opportunity to participate.

items.title: Self-Hosted Industry Engagement Participation
items.text:
this is incomplete

FedRAMP will engage with all stakeholders regarding self-hosted and hybrid-hosted requirements via the FedRAMP Request for Comment (RFC) process. The RFC processes ensures equal access and consideration for all stakeholders.

In addition, FedRAMP has offered the opportunity for direct engagement to a subset of key FedRAMP stakeholders as follows:

  • Cloud service providers with existing FedRAMP Certifications at Class C or Class D who have at least 15 agency uses on record by FedRAMP and appear to operate their own datacenter facilities based on the information readily available to FedRAMP. FedRAMP identified 12 qualifying cloud service providers and asked them if they would like to participate and 4 responded in the affirmative.

  • Independent assessment services that have assessed more than 20 total cloud service offerings. This is a change from RFC-0033 which proposed direct engagement only with independent assessment services of the qualifying cloud service providers. 8 independent assessment services will be asked to participate.
